question: In which of the following patients would enalapril be the best first line agent for high blood pressure control ?

options.opa: A 62 year old man with renal artery stenosis
options.opc: A 41 year old woman with hyperkalemia

analysis: Enalapril, an ACE inhibitor, is generally contraindicated in pregnancy and in patients with renal artery stenosis due to the risk of further renal impairment and fetal developmental issues. It is also not suitable for patients with hyperkalemia as it can increase potassium levels. However, it is often recommended for diabetic patients as it can provide renal protection in addition to controlling high blood pressure.
